## Historical audit: S0136

**Scope.** Only chunk 2 of 2 is visible. Citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. The referenced images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal and initial build — line 19, student `model_request`, characters [0,135985) | The stated task was to reconstruct a single indoor RGB photograph in SceneAct and Blender. The student’s code interprets it as a kitchen and builds separate architecture, columns, island, hood, cabinetry and oven assemblies. This is the student’s interpretation, not independent identification of the photograph. |
| Parts and finishes — line 19, same event and offsets | The code contains multiple meshes, solid island panels and drawers, sink components, a grouped faucet, hood components and oven parts. It assigns procedural wood grain, surface roughness and a metallic faucet treatment. Grouping establishes intended relationships, but neither names nor code alone verify physical contact, complete connections or geometric fidelity. |
| Autonomous revision — line 19, same event and offsets | After step 1, the student estimated that the post and island framing were wrong, changed camera pose and moved the hood. After step 2, it diagnosed the left wall as blocking sightlines and moved the wall and foreground post, while expanding surrounding architecture. These are student diagnoses and executed code changes, not independently verified image comparisons. |
| Validation and selection — line 19, same event and offsets; lines 21–22 [0,349), [0,59) | All three runs report `ok: true` and `render_available`. The student selected step 3, and a `select` event records it. This establishes execution and selection, not visual correctness. Step 2’s alleged wall occlusion was a camera/geometry issue; whether step 3 fixed it, or whether lighting and broad tones match, remains unverified here. No articulated pose is evidenced; object and camera placement are specified. |
| Input and constraints — line 19, same event and offsets; line 20, `codex_session` [0,4297) | The visible input includes system procedure and runner feedback requesting comparisons and narrow revisions. No separate teacher diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk, so teacher detection, receipt and adoption cannot be established. The final selection session was read-only, with tools disabled and zero tool calls; the preceding code-and-render cycle is visible in the supplied history. |

**Outcome and lessons.** Formal execution succeeded for three builds and step 3 was selected; reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not independently established. There is no visible empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption. A transferable observation is the separation of a scene-wide camera revision from a later local occluder correction, each followed by a reported render. The particular wall, post and hood changes are task-specific. Whether the wall caused the claimed obstruction, whether parts truly connect, and whether the final framing, materials, lighting and occlusion match the reference remain unresolved without inspecting the images and geometry. Unseen chunks may contain additional teacher input or evidence.
